content.title: 11 must-see movies this spring, from Zendaya to ‘Star Wars’
content.text: “The Drama” stars Zendaya, right, and Robert Pattinson as an engaged couple whose wedding plans collapse after a mysterious confession.A24Bookended by two science fiction films and featuring movies directed by Steven Soderbergh, James Cameron and Oakland’s Boots Riley, the spring lineup of movies has a lot to offer.And we haven’t even mentioned Zendaya, the East Bay-raised superstar whose apparent quest to dominate world cinema begins next month with the first of four major releases.Get Digital Access and Stay Informed With Trusted Local News.Get Digital Access and Stay Informed With Trusted Local News.ONLY 25¢Here are 11 of the most anticipated films of the season:Article continues below this ad‘Project Hail Mary’Ryan Gosling is a brilliant scientist-turned-astronaut who meets his own adorable E.T. while on a space mission to save humanity in Phil Lord and Christopher Miller’s terrific adaptation of a 2011 novel by Bay Area science-fiction writer Andy Weir (“The Martian”). German actor Sandra Hüller (Oscar-nominated for “Anatomy of a Fall”) also impresses as the no-nonsense official in charge of the project. San Francisco Chronicle LogoMake us a Preferred Source to get more of our news when you search.Add Preferred SourceSee this one in a theater if possible.Article continues below this adIn theaters Friday, March 20.Co-director Daniel Roher in the documentary “The AI Doc: Or How I Became an Apocaloptimist.”Focus Features‘The AI Doc: Or How I Became an Apocaloptimist’Noting that his wife is six months pregnant, filmmaker Daniel Roher (“Navalny”) wonders, with the threat of artificial intelligence, if this is even a good time to have children. “I know people who work on AI risk who don’t expect their children to make it to high school,” says Tristan Harris, co-founder of the Center for Humane Technology, in the film. Article continues below this adCo-directed by Charlie Tyrell, the movie features key Bay Area AI experts — OpenAI CEO Sam Altman and Anthropic co-founders Dario and Daniela Amodei, UC Berkeley scientist Deborah Raji, and Inflection AI co-founder Reid Hoffman — who help the filmmakers arrive at a risk assessment for a technology that is soon to take over the world.In theaters Friday, March 27.‘The Drama’Zendaya and Robert Pattinson are madly in love and days away from their wedding when the bride-to-be lets slip a secret from her past. Suddenly, there’s some drama to deal with in the dark romantic comedy drama by Kristoffer Borgli (“Dream Scenario”). The film hits theaters the same month that Season 3 of “Euphoria” debuts on HBO Max, so expect to see a lot of Zendaya, who later in the year will star in “The Odyssey,” “Spider-Man: Brand New Day” and “Dune: Part Three.” Article continues below this adIn theaters April 3.‘The Christophers’Steven Soderbergh’s black comedy stars Ian McKellen as a painter who was once a pop art sensation but hasn’t put brush to canvas in decades. Plus, he’s broke. His two estranged children (James Corden and “Baby Reindeer” breakout star Jessica Gunning), eager for an inheritance, hire a forger (Michaela Coel) to complete his unfinished works so they can be “discovered” after his death.In theaters April 10.“Saturday Night Live” creator Lorne Michaels is profiled in director Morgan Neville’s documentary “Lorne.”Focus Features‘Lorne’Celebrity documentarian Morgan Neville, whose Paul McCartney film “Man on the Run” premiered on Prime Video in February, is back with a profile of “Saturday Night Live” creator Lorne Michaels. Article continues below this adConsidering the number of “SNL” alums who went on to greatness, it’s not a stretch to consider this one of the most star-studded films of 2026. Weighing in on Michaels’ legend are Steve Martin, Tina Fey, Mike Myers, Conan O’Brien, Seth Meyers, Alec Baldwin and Colin Jost, just to name a few. In theaters April 17.Jafaar Jackson plays his uncle, Michael Jackson, in the biopic “Michael.”Lionsgate‘Michael’Antoine Fuqua’s highly anticipated Michael Jackson biopic stars Jaafar Jackson — the son of Jermaine Jackson, so he’s M.J.’s nephew — as the King of Pop. Is it stunt casting or inspired? Viewers will have to discover themselves.Also starring is former San Francisco theater actor Colman Domingo as Joe Jackson, the hard-driving patriarch of the Jackson clan. The film begins with the family’s humble Gary, Ind., beginnings, the Jackson Five days and Michael’s solo superstardom. It also does not shy away from Michael’s legal troubles stemming from child sex abuse allegations.In theaters April 24.Robert Aramayo, left, and Maxine Peake star in “I Swear,” the story of Tourette syndrome activist John Davidson.Graeme Hunter/Sony Pictures Classics‘I Swear’The film at the center of the recent controversy out of the British Academy of Film and Television Arts Awards is coming to U.S. theaters and aims at understanding Tourette syndrome. On Feb. 22 in London, a racial slur was directed at “Sinners” actors Delroy Lindo and Michael B. Jordan from the audience by Tourette syndrome activist John Davidson. Davidson is portrayed by Robert Aramayo, who was the upset winner for best actor at the BAFTAs and will be eligible for Oscar contention next year.In theaters April 24.Meryl Streep, left, and Anne Hathaway return in “The Devil Wears Prada 2,” which hits theaters on May 1.20th Century Studios‘The Devil Wears Prada 2’This time, Streep’s Anna Wintour-like magazine editor Miranda Priestly is navigating a new media environment, and Hathaway’s Andy is now a seasoned journalist as they combine forces once again.Original director David Frankel and screenwriter Aline Brosh McKenna, adapting Lauren Weisberger’s novel, also return.In theaters May 1.‘Billie Eilish — Hit Me Hard and Soft: The Tour (Live in 3D)’If Taylor Swift and Beyoncé can make a theatrical concert film work for them, so can Billie Eilish. But the most intriguing person behind “Hit Me Hard and Soft” might be the one behind the camera. “Avatar” and “Titanic” filmmaker James Cameron tries his hand at a concert film, with Eilish credited as co-director. The movie, Eilish’s second concert film, was shot during performances in Manchester, England, in July. In theaters May 8.Naomi Ackie, from left, Taylour Paige and Keke Palmer in Boots Riley’s “I Love Boosters,” a comedy about a fearless crew of Bay Area shoplifters who strike luxury goods stores.Neon‘I Love Boosters’Boots Riley’s first film since his astonishing 2018 debut “Sorry to Bother You,” stars Keke Palmer, Naomi Ackie, Taylour Paige and Poppy Liu as part of a gang of shoplifters hitting Bay Area luxury goods stores and drawing the ire of a fashion mogul played by Demi Moore. It’s class warfare at the retail level in this socially driven comedy.In theaters May 22.“Star Wars: The Mandalorian and Grogu” is due in theaters on May 22.Disney/Lucasfilm‘Star Wars: The Mandalorian and Grogu’Lucasfilm’s long-awaited feature film continuation of the popular Disney+ series hit big screens for what is — believe it or not — the first “Star Wars” movie since “Episode IX — The Rise of Skywalker” closed out the sequel trilogy seven years ago. Datebook PicksPedro Pascal returns to the role that made him a breakout star, as the protector of the young alien nicknamed Baby Yoda (though he is not, in fact, Yoda). Sigourney Weaver joins the cast after being seen in December in “Avatar: Fire and Ash.”In theaters May 22.Correction: An earlier version of this story misstated the year Andy Weir’s “The Martian” was released. It was published in 2011. March 13, 2026Staff WriterG. Allen Johnson is a San Francisco Chronicle staff writer.
